ostrzezenia.tekst: According to NCHFP, pesto should be made fresh and kept in the refrigerator for no more than 3 days.
According to BfR, young wild garlic leaves resemble those of the poisonous lily of the valley and the very poisonous autumn crocus; when in doubt, it is better not to eat them.

According to AGES, wild garlic leaves may be contaminated with fox tapeworm eggs, which can cause a life-threatening disease in humans; the eggs survive usual freezing at -18 °C and are killed at around +60 °C.

akapity: According to NCHFP, pesto is an uncooked seasoning mixture that usually includes fresh basil, garlic, pine nuts and oil.
This pesto is made from raw wild garlic leaves and is not heated, and freezing does not kill fox tapeworm eggs.
According to AGES, wild garlic is also confused with spotted arum, Solomon’s seal and wild tulips.
JarAtlas rule: if you are not sure that every leaf is wild garlic, do not use the leaves.
